edit.append_context: Reconciliation: COM-038 and the behaviour half of COM-037 merged here. On a shared sender that serves several branches of one brand (PLT-025) the bot asks 'which branch?' once per conversation.
add_acceptance: Given 'Hi' from a known phone, then a menu (Book, My appointment, Talk to clinic) arrives in < 3 s p95
Given two unrecognised free-text messages in a row, then the thread is handed to reception, the patient is told a person will reply, and the bot does not reply until staff hand it back

Given 'chest pain' or another phrase from the clinically signed emergency list, then the local emergency number (108 India, 997 KSA, 998 UAE, 999 Qatar) is sent immediately and the thread is flagged urgent
Given the patient abandons after picking a time, when 2 minutes pass, then the soft hold is released
Given a clinic in request mode, when the patient confirms, then the request appears in reception.requests and the patient is told it is pending
Given an India and a KSA clinic, then date, time and currency on the confirmation card follow the clinic locale (Asia/Kolkata INR; Asia/Riyadh SAR)

ownership_notes.topic: Event naming: notification command and related events
ownership_notes.decision: The canonical command is comms.notification.requested.v1 (with comms.notification.cancelled.v1), emitted only through NotificationPort (COM-004), which writes notification_requests plus an outbox event carrying ids only (claim check). doc 06's 'notification.requested' is an alias and is retired: ADM, CLN, FIN, HOS and PHL stories that wrote 'notification.requested' use the canonical name. Inbound messages are comms.inbound.received.v1 (COM-030); entitlement changes are platform.entitlements.changed.v1 (PLT-059); privacy notices organization.privacy_notice.published.v1 (IDC-003/025). New names are registered in the T-079 event catalogue.
ownership_notes.rationale: Matches the <module>.<entity>.<verb>.v1 rule in the brief and gives one contract owner (COM) for all senders.

ownership_notes.topic: Patient Access Edge and WhatsApp bot ownership
ownership_notes.decision: Patient Access (ACC) owns services/patient-edge: the service, its database, the conversation framework and the booking, family, registration, reminder-landing, status and GA flows (ACC-038..045). Comms (COM) owns sending, templates, webhooks, inbox, STOP, reminder scheduling and the provider stub. COM's remaining Edge flows (COM-016, 041, 045, 047, 049, 050, 051) are built on ACC-039 and reviewed by ACC as code owner.
ownership_notes.rationale: Brief and ADR-01: conversation logic lives in patient-edge and sending in comms-gateway; tracker Team for T-120/162/165/166/189 is Patient Access.

ownership_notes.decision: staff-web calls Core /v1/inbox/**; Core checks staff auth, tenant and permission, writes audit and PHI read logs, then calls the Comms Gateway internal API over mTLS (aud=internal). Comms never validates staff JWTs. New messages reach screens through the core.realtime SSE topic inbox:{tenantId}.
ownership_notes.rationale: Keeps one staff identity and audit path (ADR-06/07); Comms stays contract-only with no staff session handling.

ownership_notes.decision: ACC owns the SSE endpoint, fan-out and /v1/queue/board (ACC-021, ACC-022); FEF owns the browser client (FEF-020); OPS owns Valkey sizing, the probe dashboards and the later extraction into a stateless service (OPS-024).
ownership_notes.rationale: T-094 is a Patient Access task; doc 06 lists realtime under Platform & Trust, but splitting one endpoint across two squads would duplicate the build.

ownership_notes.topic: Inpatient and ER visit record (reuse of queue_entries)
ownership_notes.decision: Hospital admissions and ER visits reuse queue_entries as the encounter segment (class 'ambulatory' | 'inpatient' | 'emergency') so notes, prescriptions, orders and invoices keep their FKs. Core visit (Patient Access) stays the single writer: HOS opens segments through VisitCommands, and ACC-022 owns the class='ambulatory' filter and partial index on every OPD queue, board and ETA query. If Clinical later splits ENCOUNTER out, admissions.encounter_id and er_visits.encounter_id move with it.
ownership_notes.rationale: Avoids a parallel encounter table in Phase 5 and keeps ADR-02 single-writer table ownership.

ownership_notes.decision: FEF scaffolds apps/patient-web once (FEF-061: shell, i18n, secure-link auth, tokens). After the scaffold Patient Access owns the app in CODEOWNERS (doc 06 §8.1); IDC (secure links, consent approvals), ACC (booking, live queue, aggregator) and COM add features on it.
ownership_notes.rationale: One shell built by the UI guild; ownership then follows doc 06 §8.1 so no squad scaffolds a second app.

ownership_notes.decision: DSR intake/export, erasure, retention clocks and legal hold live in core module 'patient' (package patient/internal/privacy) and are owned by Platform & Trust privacy operations (PLT-047..049). No new 'privacy' module for now. IDC keeps consent capture, notices, the correction flow (IDC-022) and the exchange; COM keeps the WhatsApp intake flow (COM-051); ADM keeps the compliance card (ADM-033).
ownership_notes.rationale: Erasure and retention act on patient-owned data; ADR-01/02 discourage new modules; T-237/T-238 are Platform & Trust tasks.

ownership_notes.decision: Data & Infra (OPS) chooses and runs the regional OLAP store per cell, starting with the Postgres analytics replica (OPS-011) and moving to ClickHouse only on measured need; CDC comes from OPS-019. ADM-045/046 build chain models and dashboards on it; HOS-017/HOS-055 read it. OPS-010 owns the in-database rollups.
ownership_notes.rationale: ADR-01: reporting becomes CDC to OLAP; infra/data-platform is an OPS module and the store must stay in-region (ADR-09).

ownership_notes.decision: PLT-016 (iam) owns the column, backfill and ActorDirectory read, pulled into S2 so CLN-005 can use it. Clinical sets the flag from verified licence data only through iam.api; ADM, ACC and HOS read it via ActorDirectory for doctor pickers, rosters and OT lists.
ownership_notes.rationale: T-305 is a Platform & Trust task and iam owns staff (doc 06 §4.4); one writer avoids the role-name ILIKE problem coming back.

ownership_notes.rationale: doc 06 §4.4 makes pharmacy the single writer of stock; ADR-01 rejects parallel engines.
